decisions.reason: Clarifying that the module has 40 pins rather than the development board's 44 duplicated pins does not change any existing GPIO assignment.
The module pin-count clarification does not necessarily alter the main-board dimensions, component placement, connector placement, or mechanical arrangement.
The 40-pin count concerns the ESP32 module breakout, not the main board's JST or USB connector inventory.
The clarification does not change the required panel controls, their connector-based implementation, or their GPIO mappings.
The ESP32 module pin count has no necessary effect on the selected monitoring IC, monitored rails, channel count, or monitor placement.
The distinction between development-board and module pin counts does not change LED supply voltage, data-level handling, power control, or LED model.
The module pin-count clarification does not affect standalone USB activation, LDO capacity, powered scope, or the unresolved LDO adequacy issue.
The sensor-board connector topology and pinouts remain unchanged by the ESP32 module's clarified physical pin count.
The module pin-count clarification does not change the charge-status indicator, its GPIO, connector, or resistor configuration.
The clarified ESP32 module pin count does not alter the sensor board's orientation, dimensions policy, connector alignment, or component arrangement.
The distinction between duplicated development-board pins and the module's 40 pins does not remove or modify the local decoupling requirement.
The module pin-count clarification has no necessary effect on the power sources, OR-ing method, diode requirement, or source-selection behavior.
